description: Intent i020 (SNAPSHOT=s04, BRANCH=gro-frag-stale-ptr) complete. Searched only snapshots/s04: GRO core frag0 lifecycle (net/core/gro.c skb_gro_reset_offset/gro_pull_from_frag0/dev_gro_receive/napi_frags_skb), include/net/gro.h header helpers (skb_gro_header/slow, tcp_gro_pull_header), and all main *_gro_receive/_gro_complete/_gso_segment handlers (tcp_offload, tcpv6_offload, ip6_offload, udp_offload, af_inet inet_gro_receive, gre_offload, fou_core gue_gro_receive, drivers/net/geneve.c, drivers/net/vxlan/vxlan_core.c). FINDING (medium confidence): s04:net/ipv4/udp_offload.c:178-207, __skb_udp_tunnel_segment() — untrusted source is UDP-tunnel GSO super-packets (vxlan/geneve/fou software segmentation) whose outer UDP header bytes are packet-supplied; struct udphdr *uh = udp_hdr(skb) captured at line 181 is held across pskb_may_pull(skb, tnl_hlen) at line 189 (tnl_hlen spans the region including the UDP header), which for a cloned/non-linear skb calls __pskb_pull_tail -> pskb_expand_head and frees/replaces skb->head; the stale pre-pull uh is then dereferenced at line 199 (uh->len) and line 202 (uh->check) to compute the 'partial' checksum that is written into every segment's uh->check at line 292 — reads through potentially freed slab memory whose result becomes transmitted packet bytes, the same head-relocation UAF class as the seed's pep_get_sb(). No refetch occurs until line 275, after gso_inner_segment. Twelve candidates triaged: 1 reported (the finding), 11 safe (tcp_gro_pull_header and tcp4/tcp6/ipv6/inet/gre/gue/geneve gro handlers all refetch via skb_gro_header_slow or re-derive after pulls; udp_gro_receive_segment reads uh before its flist pull; vxlan gro wrappers hold no pointers; gro.c frag0 cursor is adjusted after gro_pull_from_frag0). Limitations: static analysis only, no KASAN reproducer — the finding requires a cloned/non-linear UDP-tunnel GSO skb for pskb_expand_head to actually free the head; ~30 drivers/ gro/gso files (sctp, esp4/esp6, mpls_gso, nsh, xfrm_iptfs, stmmac, sunvnet, niu, ipoib, t7xx, netvsc, etc.) were only pattern-screened within the triage bound; impact limited to checksum corruption/info-leak of freed-head bytes into transmitted segments; no network access to compare against upstream fixes.
